issues.body: added_npm_package() returns the first matching manifest, build_context() creates one package context, and _new_public_package_added() checks only that same package. A PR adding two public packages therefore creates follow-ons for just one and silently omits the other; if the first manifest is private and a later one is public, all three rules are suppressed. The test named test_private_marker_only_exempts_the_added_package explicitly limits itself to public-first ordering and does not establish the claimed coverage for every new public package.
issues.fix_hint: Evaluate matching manifests per package and emit templates once for each newly added public package, with package-specific context and dedup keys. Add tests for two public packages and for private-first/public-second ordering.
issues.title: Only the first newly added npm package receives follow-ons

issues.body: unless_paths = ["site/**"] and ["book/**"] veto the whole rule on any change in those trees. A PR can add a public package while merely fixing an unrelated site component or guide typo, and no advertisement/guide issue will be filed even though the new package remains undocumented. This contradicts the descriptions that suppression means the PR already did the follow-on's work.
issues.fix_hint: Use a package-specific proof of coverage (for example, inspect the canonical surface registry and SUMMARY/guide entry for the resolved package) or avoid suppression unless the exact expected files/content are present. Add negative tests where unrelated site/** and book/** changes must not suppress follow-ons.
issues.title: Any unrelated site or book change suppresses the package documentation follow-on

verdict.summary: The new follow-on mechanism misses required work in two ordinary PR shapes: it evaluates only the first added npm manifest, and it suppresses documentation follow-ons when any file in the corresponding tree changes, even if that change is unrelated to the new package. The tests encode these behaviors rather than covering the intended per-package and package-specific obligations.
